description: The Space Networks Regulatory Hub of the ITU Radiocommunication Bureau publishes the information on satellite networks and systems that the Radio Regulations require, for the international coordination and recording of satellite frequencies and orbital positions. It lists satellite networks and their frequency assignments filed by national administrations for geostationary and non-geostationary orbits, with lists of networks brought into use or suspended, non-geostationary constellations under the milestone-based approach of Resolution 35, changes of notifying administration and names, and comments on filings; tools include ITU Space Explorer for exploring network characteristics, the BR IFIC space services online, as-received filings and the Notex query. Coverage: all satellite network filings worldwide, updated with each fortnightly BR IFIC. Format and access: web lists and query tools free of charge; the BR IFIC databases on DVD or download need a subscription or ITU account for some parts. Caveats: filings describe planned networks, many never built; the data model is complex and regulatory. Simulation uses: spectrum and orbital planning context for satellite communications, and inventories of planned constellations for capacity and interference studies. Related records: CelesTrak and DISCOS give objects actually in orbit.
